## ObjectReferenceVariant type

What a typed single-object output position holds: a bound reference to one `T`<!-- -->, in either form.

**Signature:**

```typescript
type ObjectReferenceVariant<T, Id = unknown, R extends string = string> =
  | IdentityReference<T, Id, R>
  | SelectorReference<T, R>
```

**References:** [IdentityReference](./contracts.identityreference.md)<!-- -->, [SelectorReference](./contracts.selectorreference.md)

## Remarks

A typed position holds both forms of its cardinality, so its value is this union rather than one form. An input position takes the data form instead ([ObjectReferenceData](./contracts.objectreferencedata.md)<!-- -->), to which this type is assignable. Narrow on `form` to reach the identifier or the selector. Broad consumers that only resolve can use [ObjectReference](./contracts.objectreference.md) instead.
